generatedBy.purpose: Reduce human sense-selection and child-definition drafting effort; suggestions remain unreviewed.

suggestions.proposedChildDefinition: A sort is a group or type of things that share something in common.
suggestions.proposedChildExample: This sort of fruit grows in summer.
suggestions.rationale: Category or kind is the ordinary child-facing noun; approximate-description and person-type readings are secondary.

suggestions.proposedChildDefinition: Speed tells how fast something moves by comparing distance with time.
suggestions.proposedChildExample: The bicycle's speed increased on the smooth road.
suggestions.rationale: Distance travelled per unit time is the clearest school meaning; general event rate and hurrying are distinct.

suggestions.proposedChildDefinition: Quick means happening or being done in a short time.
suggestions.rationale: Rapid completion without delay is the ordinary adjective reading; hurried-brief and agile-motion senses are narrower.

suggestions.proposedChildDefinition: Clean means free from dirt or unwanted material.
suggestions.proposedChildExample: Wash your hands until they are clean.
suggestions.rationale: Freedom from dirt or impurities is the foundational meaning; unrestricted and sound/color senses are specialized.

suggestions.proposedChildDefinition: A computer is an electronic machine that processes information and follows instructions.
suggestions.proposedChildExample: We used the computer to type our project.
suggestions.rationale: The machine sense is the ordinary modern child meaning; the historical human-calculator sense is secondary.

suggestions.proposedChildDefinition: A hotel is a place where travelers can pay to stay for a short time.
suggestions.proposedChildExample: The family stayed at a hotel during the trip.
suggestions.rationale: Only supplied candidate and the ordinary lodging meaning.

suggestions.proposedChildDefinition: A beach is an area of sand or small stones beside a sea or lake.
suggestions.proposedChildExample: We collected shells on the beach.
suggestions.rationale: Only supplied candidate and an unambiguous primary geography meaning.

suggestions.proposedChildDefinition: Color is the visual quality that makes things appear red, blue, green, or other shades.
suggestions.proposedChildExample: The leaf changed color from green to yellow.
suggestions.rationale: Visual color is the ordinary early-primary meaning; vividness and musical timbre are specialized.

suggestions.proposedChildDefinition: A shop is a place where people buy goods or services.
suggestions.proposedChildExample: We bought pencils from the shop.
suggestions.rationale: Retail establishment is the ordinary child-facing noun; workshop and trade-class meanings are secondary.

suggestions.proposedChildDefinition: A camera is a device used to take photographs or record images.
suggestions.proposedChildExample: Dad used the camera to take a picture.
suggestions.rationale: General photographic-camera sense fits the child vocabulary target better than the specialized television-camera sense.

suggestions.proposedChildDefinition: A lake is a body of water surrounded by land.
suggestions.proposedChildExample: Boats moved across the calm lake.
suggestions.rationale: Geographic water-body sense is unambiguous for children; the other candidates are pigment senses.

suggestions.proposedChildDefinition: An adult is a fully grown person.
suggestions.proposedChildExample: An adult helped the children cross the road.
suggestions.rationale: Mature person is the general social meaning; mature animal is a distinct science sense.

suggestions.proposedChildDefinition: A window is an opening with glass in a wall or roof that lets in light and may let in air.
suggestions.proposedChildExample: Sunlight came through the classroom window.
suggestions.rationale: Building window is the ordinary child-facing noun; vehicle and transparent-panel senses are narrower.
